channel.title: Unintended Consequences Blog
channel.description: Blog posts from Unintended Consequences podcast episodes.

item.title: Reformers ended cash bail to free the poor before trial — and found that removin...
item.description: Reformers ended cash bail to free the poor before trial — and found that removing one flawed tool requires designing what comes next.

item.title: Uber set out to free drivers from taxi medallions with flexible, well-paid work ...
item.description: Uber set out to free drivers from taxi medallions with flexible, well-paid work — and left millions earning below minimum wage in algorithm-driven jobs.

item.title: Facial recognition was installed at airports to speed security and catch the rig...
item.description: Facial recognition was installed at airports to speed security and catch the right people — then the same systems started watching schools, stadiums, and protests.

item.title: Marketed as an indestructible shield against fire, asbestos fibers remained in l...
item.description: Marketed as an indestructible shield against fire, asbestos fibers remained in lungs for decades and triggered a slow epidemic of cancer that regulators could not see in time.

item.title: D.A.R.E. placed uniformed officers in classrooms to teach millions of children t...
item.description: D.A.R.E. placed uniformed officers in classrooms to teach millions of children to refuse drugs, yet repeated evaluations found the program produced little measurable change in behavior.

item.title: Plastic bag bans cut visible litter but drove shoppers to buy more trash liners ...
item.description: Plastic bag bans cut visible litter but drove shoppers to buy more trash liners and thicker “reusable” bags that often lasted no longer.

item.title: Malcolm McLean’s shipping container slashed the cost of moving goods worldwide —...
item.description: Malcolm McLean’s shipping container slashed the cost of moving goods worldwide — and emptied the working waterfronts that had sustained port cities for generations.

item.title: Zara and H&M set out to make runway fashion affordable for ordinary shoppers — a...
item.description: Zara and H&M set out to make runway fashion affordable for ordinary shoppers — and created an industry that now produces 92 million tonnes of textile waste a year while emitting 8–10% of global greenhouse gases.

item.title: Governments spent hundreds of billions fixing the Y2K bug, then concluded the th...
item.description: Governments spent hundreds of billions fixing the Y2K bug, then concluded the threat had never been real.

item.title: The Royal Navy cured scurvy with lemon juice in 1795, then quietly lost the reme...
item.description: The Royal Navy cured scurvy with lemon juice in 1795, then quietly lost the remedy as steamships and limes replaced the original practice.

item.title: Scared Straight sent at-risk teens into prisons to be confronted by inmates in t...
item.description: Scared Straight sent at-risk teens into prisons to be confronted by inmates in the hope that fear would keep them out of trouble — and later studies found the programs raised their odds of offending.

item.title: The U.S. government paid southern farmers to plant kudzu to stop erosion — and t...
item.description: The U.S. government paid southern farmers to plant kudzu to stop erosion — and the vine kept growing long after the crisis ended.

item.title: Companies adopted game mechanics to make fitness, learning, and work more engagi...
item.description: Companies adopted game mechanics to make fitness, learning, and work more engaging — and watched users chase points while real progress and well-being declined.

item.title: Twentieth-century engineers built dams to power the West and control floods, the...
item.description: Twentieth-century engineers built dams to power the West and control floods, then spent decades dismantling some so salmon could reach their spawning grounds again.

item.title: Platforms promised clean feeds for users and quietly hired tens of thousands of ...
item.description: Platforms promised clean feeds for users and quietly hired tens of thousands of moderators to deliver them, shifting the psychological cost out of sight.

item.title: US dietary guidelines urged Americans to cut fat for heart health — and watched ...
item.description: US dietary guidelines urged Americans to cut fat for heart health — and watched obesity climb as sugar filled the gap.

item.title: The 1968 National Flood Insurance Program set out to limit building in flood-pro...
item.description: The 1968 National Flood Insurance Program set out to limit building in flood-prone areas but instead subsidized far more development behind levees.

item.title: Park managers exterminated Yellowstone’s wolves to protect elk and livestock, th...
item.description: Park managers exterminated Yellowstone’s wolves to protect elk and livestock, then watched the rivers, forests, and beavers collapse in their absence.

item.title: The Federal Reserve launched quantitative easing to rescue the economy from anot...
item.description: The Federal Reserve launched quantitative easing to rescue the economy from another Depression — and ended up widening the wealth gap for a decade.

item.title: China's Three Gorges Dam promised flood control and clean power for hundreds of ...
item.description: China's Three Gorges Dam promised flood control and clean power for hundreds of millions, yet its reservoir began stressing faults and destabilizing entire hillsides.

item.title: NIST's 2003 password rules tried to make systems stronger by demanding complexit...
item.description: NIST's 2003 password rules tried to make systems stronger by demanding complexity and rotation, yet they trained users to create the very patterns attackers learned to exploit first.

item.title: Pediatric guidelines told parents to withhold peanuts until age three — and pean...
item.description: Pediatric guidelines told parents to withhold peanuts until age three — and peanut allergies rose sharply instead.

item.title: Mao's China exterminated sparrows to protect grain harvests and instead unleashe...
item.description: Mao's China exterminated sparrows to protect grain harvests and instead unleashed insect swarms that deepened the Great Famine.

item.title: Smokey Bear urged Americans to stamp out every spark — and turned manageable for...
item.description: Smokey Bear urged Americans to stamp out every spark — and turned manageable forests into fuel for megafires that now consume the agency’s budget.

item.title: The 1978 Airline Deregulation Act promised cheaper flights for everyone — and pr...
item.description: The 1978 Airline Deregulation Act promised cheaper flights for everyone — and produced an industry where four carriers now control roughly 80 percent of the market.

item.title: Post-war mortgage subsidies made homeownership reachable for millions of familie...
item.description: Post-war mortgage subsidies made homeownership reachable for millions of families — and built the car-dependent, racially segregated suburbs that later proved nearly impossible to change.

item.title: London's congestion charge cut traffic inside the zone by 15 percent — and shift...
item.description: London's congestion charge cut traffic inside the zone by 15 percent — and shifted the jams and fumes to the boroughs just beyond its boundary.

item.title: Automakers recast streets as car space and turned crossing them into a crime, re...
item.description: Automakers recast streets as car space and turned crossing them into a crime, reshaping cities for a century.

item.title: St. Louis built Pruitt-Igoe in 1954 as a model of clean, modern public housing f...
item.description: St. Louis built Pruitt-Igoe in 1954 as a model of clean, modern public housing for working families — and dynamited the first buildings on national television in 1972.

item.title: Eisenhower’s 1956 Interstate Highway Act promised faster travel for all, yet in ...
item.description: Eisenhower’s 1956 Interstate Highway Act promised faster travel for all, yet in city after city the new roads accelerated the emptying of urban neighborhoods instead.

item.title: Synthetic fabrics promised cheap, durable clothes for everyone — and released tr...
item.description: Synthetic fabrics promised cheap, durable clothes for everyone — and released trillions of plastic fibers that now reach every human placenta and ocean trench.

item.title: A synthetic estrogen given to millions of pregnant women to prevent miscarriage ...
item.description: A synthetic estrogen given to millions of pregnant women to prevent miscarriage instead caused rare reproductive cancers in their daughters two decades later.

item.title: Mosquito nets built to save millions from malaria are instead being cut into fis...
item.description: Mosquito nets built to save millions from malaria are instead being cut into fishing gear that empties lakes and leaks insecticide into the water.

item.title: Europe and the US mandated biofuels to cut transport emissions, then watched pal...
item.description: Europe and the US mandated biofuels to cut transport emissions, then watched palm-oil plantations clear rainforests faster than before.

item.title: Hospitals championed alcohol sanitizers to curb deadly infections, yet everyday ...
item.description: Hospitals championed alcohol sanitizers to curb deadly infections, yet everyday overuse may be nudging antimicrobial resistance forward.

item.title: Millions of women took hormone replacement therapy to prevent heart disease and ...
item.description: Millions of women took hormone replacement therapy to prevent heart disease and stay youthful, until one trial showed it raised their risks of cancer, stroke, and heart attack instead.

item.title: Purdue Pharma promoted OxyContin as nearly addiction-proof, yet the drug helped ...
item.description: Purdue Pharma promoted OxyContin as nearly addiction-proof, yet the drug helped ignite an opioid epidemic that has killed more than a million Americans.

item.title: Factories added radium to watch dials so soldiers could read time in the dark — ...
item.description: Factories added radium to watch dials so soldiers could read time in the dark — then trained the painters to shape brushes between their lips.

item.title: António Egas Moniz won the 1949 Nobel Prize for the prefrontal lobotomy, a proce...
item.description: António Egas Moniz won the 1949 Nobel Prize for the prefrontal lobotomy, a procedure that soon left tens of thousands with lasting cognitive damage.

item.title: A sedative promoted as safe for pregnant women in the 1950s produced the largest...
item.description: A sedative promoted as safe for pregnant women in the 1950s produced the largest drug-related birth-defect epidemic on record before testing rules changed.

item.title: Europe's GDPR required websites to obtain clear consent for tracking cookies — a...
item.description: Europe's GDPR required websites to obtain clear consent for tracking cookies — and produced an internet full of banners that almost no one reads.

item.title: Congress set stricter fuel economy rules for cars than light trucks in 1975, and...
item.description: Congress set stricter fuel economy rules for cars than light trucks in 1975, and automakers responded by selling millions of SUVs instead.

item.title: Daylight Saving Time was introduced to conserve coal and oil, yet modern evidenc...
item.description: Daylight Saving Time was introduced to conserve coal and oil, yet modern evidence shows it saves almost no energy while raising heart attacks and crashes.

item.title: Western aid meant to build self-sufficient African economies instead left many g...
item.description: Western aid meant to build self-sufficient African economies instead left many governments dependent on the next foreign transfer to stay afloat.

item.title: The No Child Left Behind Act tied federal funding to test scores to help every c...
item.description: The No Child Left Behind Act tied federal funding to test scores to help every child succeed and instead narrowed what millions of students were taught.

item.title: Rent control was meant to shield tenants from unaffordable rents, yet it repeate...
item.description: Rent control was meant to shield tenants from unaffordable rents, yet it repeatedly reduced the supply of rental housing and raised prices for everyone else.

item.title: China's one-child policy aimed to ease population pressure but instead produced ...
item.description: China's one-child policy aimed to ease population pressure but instead produced a 30-million-person gender imbalance and a shrinking workforce that will shape the country for decades.

item.title: Cash for Clunkers paid Americans to destroy nearly 700,000 old cars in 2009 to r...
item.description: Cash for Clunkers paid Americans to destroy nearly 700,000 old cars in 2009 to revive the economy, but it left low-income buyers facing higher used-car prices for years.

item.title: Nixon declared the War on Drugs in 1971 to protect families by treating addictio...
item.description: Nixon declared the War on Drugs in 1971 to protect families by treating addiction as crime; five decades later the U.S. prison population had grown sixfold while drug-use rates stayed roughly unchanged.

item.title: California's three-strikes law promised to lock up dangerous repeat offenders — ...
item.description: California's three-strikes law promised to lock up dangerous repeat offenders — and instead gave life sentences for stealing pizza and videotapes.
